turns.t: Morning, doctor. I'm sorry to come about this, but I've got this awful pain in my face, on the right, when I chew. It's like an electric shock.
Tell me more about it. How long has it been going on?
Two weeks. It started with a shooting pain in my cheek, when I was brushing my teeth, and it's been coming and going ever since.
How long does each attack last?
A few seconds. Maybe ten. It's sharp, and then it's gone, and I'm left waiting for the next one.
What sets it off?
Chewing, brushing my teeth, a cold breeze on my face, even talking, sometimes.
Where exactly is the pain?
Along the cheek, to the corner of my mouth, and my upper jaw, on the right.
Any pain between the attacks, or toothache?
No pain in between. And my teeth are fine, I've seen the dentist, who found nothing.
Any numbness, or weakness of the face, or changes in your vision?
No, none of those.
Any previous health conditions?
High blood pressure, that's all.
Anyone in the family with similar pain?
My aunt had a nerve thing in her face, I think.
Any allergies to medicines?
Years ago, carbamazepine, I think I broke out in a rash, so I haven't had it since.
That's important, thank you. Let me check your numbers. ~
Go on. ~
Pulse 72, blood pressure 140 over 86, temperature 36.6.
Is that high? ~
Slightly, but fine. Now I'll test the feeling in your face. Close your eyes. ~
Okay.
The feeling is normal on both sides of the face, your jaw muscles are strong, and I can trigger a shooting pain by lightly touching the right cheek.
That's the one. ~
What you describe, brief electric-shock pains in the cheek and jaw, triggered by touch, chewing and cold air, with a normal examination, fits trigeminal neuralgia, a condition of the facial nerve.
Is it serious? ~
It's very painful, but not dangerous. It's treatable. ~
How? ~
There's a medicine for nerve pain, but the usual first choice, carbamazepine, is the one that gave you a rash. So I'd like to start you on a different one, gabapentin.
Will it make me sleepy? ~
It can. Start with 300 mg at night, and we'll increase it slowly.
Okay. ~
Avoid triggers where you can, a scarf over your face in cold air, chew on the left, and brush gently.
Right. ~
I'd like to see you in two weeks to see how it's working.
Two weeks. Thank you. ~
